texts.preamble: Richard Shivaji Roa Holkar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh Through Food ... on 26 September, 2025 Author: Subodh Abhyankar Bench: Subodh Abhyankar Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:28555 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Indore Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice Subodh Abhyankar On The 26th Of September, 2025 Misc. Criminal Case No. 36383 of 2025 Richard Shivaji Roa Holkar Versus The State Of Madhya Pradesh Through Food Safety Officer Food And Drug Aministration Department Appearance: Shri Avinash Sirpurkar- Senior Advocate with Shri Harsh Advocate for the petitioner . Shri Hemant Sharma- G.A. for the State.
texts.arguments: 3] Shri Avinash Sirpurkar, learned senior counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner was granted permanent exemption on 16.05.2019, copy of which, is also filed on record, wherein, his application for permanent exemption has been accepted, with a further direction that as and when directed, he shall appear before the Court. Learned senior counsel has submitted that the case was fixed for delivery of judgement on 28.06.2025, on which date, an application for exemption from appearance was filed, which was accepted, however, the petitioner was directed to appear on 03.07.2025, i.e., after five days. 1 4] Shri Avinash Sirpurkar, learned senior counsel for the petitioner has also NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:28555 2 MCRC-36383-2025 submitted that the petitioner was abroad at the time when he was required to appear in the Court, and thus, he could not mark his appearance, and he is ready to appear before the Court as and when directed. It is submitted that only on one date, the petitioner could not appear due to the aforesaid fact. It is further submitted that the petitioner is a reputed person, and is the owner of the place where the restaurant was being run by the other accused persons, and a case under Section 31(1) of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 has been slapped against him.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 3] Shri Avinash Sirpurkar, learned senior counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner was granted permanent exemption on 16.05.2019, copy of which, is also filed on record, wherein, his application for permanent exemption has been accepted, with a further direction that as and when directed, he shall appear before the Court. Learned senior counsel has submitted that the case was fixed for delivery of judgement on 28.06.2025, on which date, an application for exemption from appearance was filed, which was accepted, however, the petitioner was directed to appear on 03.07.2025, i.e., after five days. 1 4] Shri Avinash Sirpurkar, learned senior counsel for the petitioner has also NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:28555 2 MCRC-36383-2025 submitted that the petitioner was abroad at the time when he was required to appear in the Court, and thus, he could not mark his appearance, and he is ready to appear before the Court as and when directed. It is submitted that only on one date, the petitioner could not appear due to the aforesaid fact. It is further submitted that the petitioner is a reputed person, and is the owner of the place where the restaurant was being run by the other accused persons, and a case under Section 31(1) of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 has been slapped against him.
